subject: Chemistry
title: Valence Bond Theory (VBT): Hybridization & Complex Geometry
topics: Linus Pauling's Valence Bond Theory (VBT) Principles & Orbital Hybridization
CN = 4 (sp³ Tetrahedral vs dsp² Square Planar) and CN = 6 (d²sp³ Inner Octahedral vs sp³d² Outer Octahedral)
Inner Orbital Complexes (d²sp³, Low-Spin/Spin-Paired) vs Outer Orbital Complexes (sp³d², High-Spin/Spin-Free)
Spin-Only Magnetic Moments (μ_s = √(n(n+2)) BM) across VBT Configurations
quickSummary: VBT uses orbital hybridization: CN=4 is sp³ (tetrahedral) or dsp² (square planar); CN=6 is d²sp³ (inner orbital, low-spin) or sp³d² (outer orbital, high-spin). Strong field ligands (CN⁻, CO, NH₃) force electron pairing. [Ni(CO)₄] has Ni⁰ in sp³ (diamagnetic); [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is dsp² square planar (diamagnetic); [NiCl₄]²⁻ is sp³ tetrahedral (paramagnetic, n=2).
summary: Master Valence Bond Theory hybridization, inner/outer orbital configurations, geometry predictions, and magnetic moments.

summaryBox.title: VBT Hybridization Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: CN=4: sp³ (tetrahedral, 109.5°) vs dsp² (square planar, 90°). CN=6: d²sp³ (inner orbital, low-spin) vs sp³d² (outer orbital, high-spin).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VBT HYBRIDIZATION & GEOMETRY
                       
   CN = 4 ──► $sp^3$ (Tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$)  OR  $dsp^2$ (Square Planar, $90^\circ$)
   CN = 6 ──► $d^2sp^3$ (Inner Orbital Octahedral) OR  $sp^3d^2$ (Outer Orbital Octahedral)

                    INNER ORBITAL vs OUTER ORBITAL COMPLEXES
                    
   INNER ORBITAL COMPLEX ($d^2sp^3$): Uses **inner $(n-1)d$ orbitals**. Strong field ligands ($\text{CN}^-, \text{NH}_3$)
                                      force electron pairing $\implies$ **Low-Spin / Spin-Paired**.
                                      
   OUTER ORBITAL COMPLEX ($sp^3d^2$): Uses **outer $nd$ orbitals**. Weak field ligands ($\text{F}^-, \text{H}_2\text{O}$)
                                      cannot force pairing $\implies$ **High-Spin / Spin-Free**.
conceptBreakdown.content: Proposed by Linus Pauling, VBT assumes that the central metal ion provides vacant $d, s, p$ hybrid orbitals to accept lone pairs donated by ligands.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VBT COMPLEX PROFILES MATRIX

• [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻: Fe²⁺ (3d⁶), Strong CN⁻ ──► d²sp³ Inner Octahedral, n=0, Diamagnetic
• [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵), Strong CN⁻ ──► d²sp³ Inner Octahedral, n=1, Paramagnetic (1.73 BM)
• [FeF₆]³⁻:    Fe³⁺ (3d⁵), Weak F⁻   ──► sp³d² Outer Octahedral, n=5, Paramagnetic (5.92 BM)
• [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: Co³⁺ (3d⁶), Strong NH₃ ──► d²sp³ Inner Octahedral, n=0, Diamagnetic
• [CoF₆]³⁻:    Co³⁺ (3d⁶), Weak F⁻   ──► sp³d² Outer Octahedral, n=4, Paramagnetic (4.90 BM)
• [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻: Ni²⁺ (3d⁸), Strong CN⁻ ──► dsp² Square Planar, n=0, Diamagnetic
• [NiCl₄]²⁻:   Ni²⁺ (3d⁸), Weak Cl⁻  ──► sp³ Tetrahedral, n=2, Paramagnetic (2.83 BM)
• [Ni(CO)₄]:   Ni⁰  (3d¹⁰), Strong CO ──► sp³ Tetrahedral, n=0, Diamagnetic
conceptBreakdown.content: Review each landmark coordination complex's central metal oxidation state, $d^n$ count, hybridization, geometry, and magnetic properties.

quickRevision: CN=6: d²sp³ (inner, low-spin) or sp³d² (outer, high-spin).
[Ni(CO)₄] is sp³ tetrahedral and diamagnetic (Ni⁰ is 3d¹⁰ 4s⁰).
[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is dsp² square planar and diamagnetic.
[NiCl₄]²⁻ is sp³ tetrahedral and paramagnetic (n=2, 2.83 BM).
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is d²sp³ diamagnetic; [CoF₆]³⁻ is sp³d² paramagnetic (n=4, 4.90 BM).
